findings.reason: the section names a source that does not exist, so a node implementing §2 must invent peer-name resolution or ship an empty field; the author must either cite the real source (the run row's `member`) or drop the peer-name claim.
findings.text: §2 states the answer "carries both facts: the plan-owner person and the coordinator session with its peer name where `reckon/crew/directory.py` resolves one", but directory.py resolves no peer or member name anywhere: its coordinator rows carry only session, project, repository, plans, sprints, state, live_node_count, runs and transports (reckon/crew/directory.py:190-208), and its run-row builder `_run_row` (reckon/crew/directory.py:91-122) carries no name field either — the only name a run row carries is `member` (reckon/run_record.py:504), produced by the ledger, not by directory.py

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the changed s2 anchors resolve: reckon/ledger.py:162-165 and reckon/run_record.py:538-539 carry the `session`/`session_id` pair, reckon/run_record.py:489 is the brief-run `plan` null, and `_live_review_runs` is at reckon/crew/obligations.py:467 with the stated live-pointer-and-review-in-flight behaviour; the false cite to directory.py is reported under reasoning.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2's done-when pins each plan's expected coordinator as a literal read from the fixture rows, names the deciding row in the gate log, and carries two negative controls (a resolver returning unowned everywhere must fail the fixture test; one ignoring dispatch order must fail the A-then-B test).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section's evidence is the fixture replay recorded as evidence for the plan; no node-local or scratchpad path is named as the durable home.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the revision introduces no new symbol; the plan cites existing mechanism-named functions (`_live_review_runs`, `plan-review-of-<slug>`) and carries no plan labels or ticket numbers into names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 names `reckon/crew/directory.py` as the source of the coordinator's peer name, but that module resolves no peer or member name.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 delivers one thing: a plan's coordinator derived from the ledger, beside its recorded owner.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s2 is the root of the owner chain and both consumers declare it (s3 and s5 each list a-coordinator-sees-the-board#s2 in plan-section-depends-on), so no node reads §2 outside its closure.
